e.etymology: The Italian form of Damian, from Greek Damianos, traditionally linked to damazo, to tame. Saints Cosmas and Damian, physician brothers, spread the name.
namesakes: Damiano David (lead singer of the rock band Maneskin)

e.etymology: An Indian name most often linked to Hindi sach, truth. Some families use it as a spelling of Sachi (Shachi), the wife of the god Indra.
From a Germanic name joining ald, old, and ric, ruler. Saint Aldric was a 9th-century bishop of Le Mans in France. It is often confused with Alaric, a separate name.
A Yoruba name joining ife, love, and Oluwa, Lord or God.
The English spelling of Welsh Macsen, a form of Latin Maximus, greatest, borne by the emperor Magnus Maximus of Welsh legend. In the US it also works as a longer form of Max.
The holy city, Hebrew Yerushalayim. Tradition reads the name as city or vision of peace; scholars trace it to an older name meaning foundation of the god Shalem.

assoc.t: holy city of Judaism, Christianity and Islam

e.etymology: The English rank and title, from Late Latin capitaneus, chief, from caput, head. It had a run as a given name in the 19th-century United States.
e.note: It is a rank, so people may hear it as a title or a nickname and not as a given name.

assoc.t: Captain Morgan spiced rum, often called the Captain

e.etymology: A modern American coinage in the style of Aleah and Kaleah, readable as Leah with a Na- prefix.
An English surname, also spelled Embry, taken up as a girls' name in the 2010s beside Ember, Emery and Aubrey.
The French-based West African spelling of Sulayman, the Arabic form of Solomon, from Hebrew Shelomoh, built on shalom, peace. Solomon is a prophet in Islam.
An elaboration of Anna or Ann with the -ella ending, in line with Annabella and Stella.
A modern name in the family of Kieran, Kyrie and Cyrian. No single origin is established.
From Albanian Arbër, the medieval name for an Albanian, from Arbëria, the old name of the country.
An American name from rodeo country, carried by veteran pro bull rider Wacey Cathey. It rhymes with Casey, Lacey and Tracy.
A Scottish surname from the Borders town of Kelso, earlier Calchow, from a name meaning chalk or lime hill.
namesakes: Michael Kelso (Ashton Kutcher's character on That '70s Show; surname)

e.etymology: A modern American name that fits Rae or Ray to the -den ending of Jayden and Brayden. It also overlaps with Raiden, the Japanese thunder god known from Mortal Kombat.

e.meaning: a great multitude; a Roman army unit
e.etymology: The English word for a Roman army unit of several thousand soldiers, from Latin legio, from legere, to gather or levy.

assoc.t: the demons called Legion in the Gospel of Mark

e.note: In Mark 5:9 a host of demons says: My name is Legion, for we are many. Churchgoers will know the line.

e.etymology: A respelling of Zariah, a modern American name that echoes Azariah and Zaria. It has no single settled meaning.
Sanskrit anala means fire and names a fire deity in Hindu texts. In the US the name also sits close to Anela and Analia.
An English surname and a spelling of Kane or Cain. As a word, a cane is a walking stick or the stem of sugarcane.
e.note: Sounds identical to Cain, the Bible's first murderer, and is spelled like the walking stick.

assoc.t: cane, a walking stick; also sugar cane and candy cane
Raising Cane's, chicken finger chain, often called Cane's

e.etymology: A modern American blend that puts a Z on Ariana or extends Zaria with -ana.
An elaboration of Dalia with the -ana ending, used mainly by Spanish-speaking families. Dalia is the Spanish name of the dahlia flower.
An English surname for someone who lived on a hide, a medieval measure of land large enough to support one household.

assoc.t: Mr. Hyde, violent alter ego of Dr. Jekyll

e.note: Most people think first of Mr. Hyde, the monstrous half of Dr. Jekyll; it also sounds like the word hide.

e.etymology: A rendering of the ancient Egyptian name of Osiris, god of the afterlife and rebirth, favored in Afrocentric and Kemetic naming.
namesakes: Ausar Thompson (NBA forward for the Detroit Pistons)

e.etymology: A blend of Quinn and the -lynn ending, also readable as a feminine respelling of the Irish surname Quinlan.
A spelling of Reyansh, a modern Indian name ending in ansh, from Sanskrit amsha, a part or portion. The first element has no settled Sanskrit source.
Took off after Kitai Raige, the character played by Jaden Smith in the 2013 film After Earth.
A French name, Anaël, with the feminine Anaëlle, popular in France since the 1990s. It matches Anael, a spelling of the angel Haniel in Jewish and Christian lore.
A respelling of Anora, a medieval English form of Honora, from Latin honor, and also an Uzbek name meaning pomegranate, as in the Oscar-winning 2024 film Anora.
From Sanskrit ramani, a beautiful or charming woman, from the root ram, to delight.
A recent American coinage with the De- prefix and the -aire ending heard in Zaire and Kyaire.
